body: General-purpose code embeddings power tools for code search, classification, and retrieval. Compact transformer encoders for code typically rely on either human-written docstrings (labor-intensive and inconsistent) or mined structural signals such as execution traces (setting-specific and costly to collect). We empirically study an alternative: contrastive pretraining of small encoders with synthetically generated natural-language descriptions emphasizing code functionality and intent, paired with code in a dual-encoder framework at training and discarded at inference. We benchmark this approach against pretraining-based baselines, generalist LLMs, and embedding-specific models on eight retrieval, classification, and generation tasks across C, C++, and Java. Synthetic semantic supervision yields statistically significant gains over pretraining baselines of the same inference-time size on five of eight tasks, with parity on two more; once fine-tuned, it matches or exceeds zero-shot models two orders of magnitude larger on classification, and it stays on par with execution-aware supervision at matched pretraining data, suggesting a scalable, effective alternative to existing code-representation paradigms.
summaryZh: 本文提出了一种新颖的对比学习方法，利用合成的自然语言描述（强调代码功能和意图）与代码配对，来预训练小型Transformer编码器，用于代码表示学习。该方法在C、C++和Java代码的检索、分类和生成任务上进行了基准测试。结果显示，与同等大小的预训练基线相比，合成语义监督在八项任务中的五项上取得了统计学上的显著提升，并在另外两项上达到持平。微调后，该方法在分类任务上能媲美规模大两个数量级的零样本模型，并与基于执行的监督方法相当，证明了其作为一种可扩展、有效的代码表示范式的潜力。
